title: Git Basic Commands
description: Essential commands for daily Git work

comicStory.title: The Chef's Recipe Management

panels.text: Chef manages recipes. Old way: Write on paper, lose track of changes, can't share with team!
No history of modifications. Chaos in the kitchen!
With Git commands: git add (prepare ingredients), git commit (save recipe version)
git push (share with team), git pull (get team updates)
git log (recipe history), git diff (compare versions)
Now: Track all changes, share instantly, see complete history, debug recipe problems!

comicStory.twist: Git commands = Your kitchen management system! Each command has a specific job!
comicStory.lesson: Master these commands = Master Git! Use them together for smooth workflow!

deepDive.whatItIs: Git basic commands are the essential tools for daily development: staging changes (git add), saving versions (git commit), syncing with remote (git push/pull/fetch), and viewing history (git log/diff/show). These commands form the foundation of all Git workflows.
deepDive.whyItMatters: Without these commands, you can't save changes, collaborate with teams, or track project history. They're used hundreds of times daily by developers worldwide. Mastering them is essential for professional development.
whereUsed: Daily development: add → commit → push workflow
Team collaboration: pull updates, push changes
Debugging: use log and diff to find issues
Code review: check changes before committing
History tracking: view who changed what and when

visualExamples.title: git add - Staging Changes
visualExamples.diagram:
git add file.txt      # Add specific file
git add .             # Add all files
git add *.js          # Add all JS files
git add -A            # Add all changes

Moves: Working Directory → Staging Area

visualExamples.title: git commit - Save Changes
visualExamples.diagram:
git commit -m "Add feature"     # Commit with message
git commit -am "Update"         # Commit all tracked
git commit --amend              # Amend last commit

Creates: Permanent snapshot in Local Repo

visualExamples.title: git push/pull - Sync with Remote
visualExamples.diagram:
git push origin main    # Upload to remote
git pull origin main    # Download + merge
git fetch origin        # Download only

push: Local → Remote
pull: Remote → Local (with merge)
fetch: Remote → Local (no merge)

visualExamples.title: git log/diff - View History
visualExamples.diagram:
git log --oneline      # Compact history
git diff                # Show unstaged changes
git diff --staged       # Show staged changes
git show abc123         # Show specific commit

Use for: Debugging, tracking, reviewing

keyPoints: git commit: Save permanently (Staging → Local Repo)
git push: Upload to remote (Local → Remote)
git fetch: Download only (safer than pull)
git diff: Show changes between versions
Always check git status before committing

interactiveQA.question: What does 'git add' do?
interactiveQA.explanation: git add moves changes from Working Directory to Staging Area, preparing them for commit. Doesn't save permanently yet. Example: git add file.txt or git add .

interactiveQA.question: What does 'git commit' do?
interactiveQA.answer: Saves staged changes permanently with a message.
interactiveQA.explanation: git commit creates a permanent snapshot, records author and timestamp, generates unique commit ID, and saves to local history. Example: git commit -m "Add feature"

interactiveQA.question: What does 'git push' do?
interactiveQA.answer: Uploads local commits to remote repository.
interactiveQA.explanation: git push uploads commits to GitHub/GitLab, updates remote repository, shares with team, and creates cloud backup. Example: git push origin main

interactiveQA.question: What does 'git pull' do?
interactiveQA.explanation: git pull downloads remote changes and merges into current branch, updating local repository. Combines fetch + merge. Example: git pull origin main

interactiveQA.question: What's the difference between 'git fetch' and 'git pull'?
interactiveQA.answer: fetch downloads only, pull downloads and merges.
interactiveQA.explanation: git fetch downloads changes without merging (safe, no conflicts). git pull downloads and merges automatically (may cause conflicts). fetch is safer!

interactiveQA.question: What does 'git log' show?
interactiveQA.answer: Commit history with author, date, and message.
interactiveQA.explanation: git log shows: commit ID, author name/email, date/time, and commit message. Useful for tracking changes, debugging, and finding commits. Use --oneline for compact view.

codingChallenge.title: Git Commands Workflow
codingChallenge.scenario: You're working on a data engineering project. Simulate the complete Git command workflow: modify files, check status, stage with git add, commit with message, push to remote, and view history.
codingChallenge.problem: Create a class that simulates Git commands: modify file, add, commit, push, and view log.
codingChallenge.expectedOutput:
Modified: app.js
Staged: 1 file
Committed: Add login function
Pushed: Success
History: 1 commit
hints: Track files in different stages: working, staged, committed, remote
codingChallenge.explanation: This simulates Git commands: modify() creates changes, add() stages them, commit() saves with message, push() uploads to remote, log() shows history. In real Git: git add, git commit -m, git push, git log.

quiz.question: What does 'git add' do?
quiz.explanation: git add stages changes, moving them from Working Directory to Staging Area. Prepares files for commit but doesn't save permanently yet.

quiz.question: What does 'git commit' do?
options: Saves staged changes permanently with message
quiz.explanation: git commit saves staged changes permanently in Local Repository with a commit message. Creates a snapshot that can be reverted to anytime.

quiz.question: What does 'git push' do?
options: Uploads local commits to Remote Repository
quiz.explanation: git push uploads commits from Local Repository to Remote Repository (GitHub/GitLab), sharing work with team and creating cloud backup.

quiz.question: What does 'git pull' do?
quiz.explanation: git pull fetches remote changes and merges them into current branch, updating local repository. Combines fetch + merge in one command.

quiz.question: Difference between 'git fetch' and 'git pull'?
options: fetch = download only, pull = download + merge
quiz.explanation: git fetch downloads changes without merging (safe, no conflicts). git pull downloads and merges automatically (may cause conflicts). fetch is safer for reviewing changes first!

quiz.question: What does 'git log' show?
options: Commit history with author, date, and message
quiz.explanation: git log shows commit history including: commit ID, author name/email, date/time, and commit message. Useful for tracking changes and debugging.

quiz.question: What does 'git diff' show?
quiz.explanation: git diff shows line-by-line differences: added lines (green +), removed lines (red -), and modified files. Use before committing to review changes!

quiz.question: Best practice before pushing?
options: Always pull first to get latest changes
quiz.explanation: Always pull before pushing: 1) git pull origin main, 2) resolve conflicts if any, 3) git push origin main. Prevents conflicts and keeps in sync!

quiz.question: What does 'git show' do?
options: Shows detailed info about specific commit
quiz.explanation: git show displays detailed information about a specific commit: author, date, message, and changes made. Example: git show abc123
